clue.text: Dealer advising reduction in Shakespeare's collected works?

definitions.meaning: a trader who buys and sells old metal and junk

definitions.text: advising reduction in Shakespeare's collected works?
definitions.meaning: read as the instruction '...', cut The Merchant of Venice from the complete plays

explanation.surface: A trader recommending that the complete Shakespeare be trimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into a verb and a noun: 'scrap' (throw out) the 'Merchant' (The Merchant of Venice), which would indeed shorten Shakespeare's collected works.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in waste metal and salvage is a familiar kind of trader.

clue.text: Book choice by old village clubman

parts.note: Samuel is a book of the Old Testament
a pick is a choice, as in take your pick
wick is an old word for a village or hamlet, surviving in place names

explanation.surface: A book selected by an elderly member of a village club.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pickwick founds the Pickwick Club in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's hero is founder and chairman of a gentlemen's society, so a member of a club.

clue.text: Cotswolds girl entitled to share a drink?

definitions.meaning: the village girl in Laurie Lee's memoir of a Cotswolds childhood
she shares the title with a drink

explanation.surface: A country girl claims her right to a share of the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entitled' seems to mean having a right, but it means named in a title: Laurie Lee's Cider with Rosie, set in the Cotswolds, an area of rural England.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurie Lee's memoir names a village girl alongside a glass of apple drink in its title.

clue.text: Almost fair and fit

parts.note: fair means good-looking, so pretty
fit means healthy, so well

explanation.surface: A description of someone who is nearly attractive and healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nearly or very nearly, as in 'pretty well finished'.

clue.text: Correction is of help to credit in general

indicators.note: something that is of help to the phrase contributes to it, so the letters are a part of these words

explanation.surface: Fixing errors generally supports a writer's credibility.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'cr-EDIT IN G-eneral'; 'is of help to' signals that it forms part of those words.
explanation.definitionFit: Editing is the revision of a text to remove mistakes.

clue.text: The cat and the fiddler, as recited

indicators.note: as recited means the word is spoken, giving one that sounds the same

parts.note: a fiddler is a swindler, so a cheater

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme echo: the cat and the fiddle, read out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls 'Hey diddle diddle, the cat and the fiddle', but a fiddler here is a cheat; in a non-rhotic British accent CHEATER and CHEETAH sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is a big spotted wild feline.

clue.text: Fit counter without top

indicators.note: without top means the first letter of the word for counter is dropped

parts.note: a table or bench works as a counter

explanation.surface: A healthy worktop missing its upper part.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the 'top' of a word is its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means capable or competent to do something.

clue.text: Hours passed in filming?

parts.note: a technique where long stretches of time are compressed into a few seconds of film

explanation.surface: Wondering how long it took to shoot a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as complaining about a long shoot, but describes the technique of taking frames at intervals so hours go by on screen in seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: The photographic technique shows slow change, like a flower opening, speeded up.

clue.text: Vastly moving main story with local ingredients

indicators.note: moving suggests the letters of these words are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A touching tale built from homegrown elements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' reads as emotionally touching, but rearranges MAIN STORY and LOCAL; 'ingredients' says those letters are the raw materials.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomically means hugely, on the scale of distances between stars.

clue.text: Occult rime seems to fascinate

indicators.note: occult suggests something mysterious and hidden, telling us the letters of these words are reworked

explanation.surface: A mysterious bit of frost appears able to cast a spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occult' looks like an adjective describing the rime (frost), but it signals that the letters of RIME SEEMS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone spellbound, as a hypnotist does, is to fascinate them.

clue.text: Colour seen at first in trees

parts.note: lime is a bright yellowish-green colour

indicators.note: at first tells us to take only the opening letter of the word seen

explanation.surface: A shade first spotted among the woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Limes, or lindens, are broad-leaved trees often planted in avenues.

clue.text: Note opening item on programme

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A remark about the first act on the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: Each separate contest or turn listed on a sports or entertainment programme is one of its fixtures.

clue.text: Nothing in it, taking a very small part

indicators.note: in tells us the zero goes inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone protests they had no hand in it while playing a bit part.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota, the smallest Greek letter, is used for the tiniest amount of anything.

clue.text: Vague impression made by shortened advert

indicators.note: shortened means the word for an advert loses its final letter

parts.note: a blurb is a short promotional description, as on a book jacket

explanation.surface: A trimmed advertisement leaves the viewer with only a hazy idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A blur is something seen or remembered indistinctly, a hazy shape.

clue.text: It goes round the heart, for example

definitions.meaning: something that circulates, moving in a circuit
the heart pumps blood round the body, so it is an example of something that circulates fluid

explanation.surface: A remark on what travels round the body's central organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A circulator is a thing that moves round or keeps something moving round, as a pump does blood.

clue.text: For old ladies, it could be a transformation

definitions.text: For old ladies, it could be a transformation

parts.words: For old ladies, it could be a transformation
parts.note: a 'transformation' was the old name for a woman's hairpiece or false front of hair, so the clue describes a kind of wig

explanation.surface: A suggestion that elderly women might undergo a dramatic makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transformation' suggests a makeover, but in Victorian usage it was a lady's wig of false hair; a periwig is an old word for a wig.
explanation.definitionFit: A periwig is an elaborate wig, and a transformation was a woman's hairpiece worn to change her look.

clue.text: Souvenirs made by soldiers and shepherds

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps
to shepherd is to mind or look after, so minders

explanation.surface: Keepsakes produced by troops and sheep farmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shepherds' reads as a noun but is a verb sense: people who shepherd are minders.
explanation.definitionFit: Souvenirs are mementos that bring back memories of a place or event.

clue.text: Sharp turn needed to keep locks secure

definitions.meaning: a very tight bend in a road, doubling back on itself
a U-shaped pin used to hold hair in place

explanation.surface: A tight corner is required to protect the locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests door security, but here they are locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A road bend shaped like a U and the bent wire clip that holds hair share one name.

clue.text: Turned up by chance in legendary place

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive, so came
lot means fate or chance, as in drawing lots

explanation.surface: Someone arrived by luck at a fabled location.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's court in the Arthurian romances is a famous mythical location.

clue.text: Stops car under the terrace

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the car's word is placed below the terrace's

parts.note: Ter. is a standard address abbreviation for Terrace
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: Parking a car beneath a row of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: TER, the abbreviation for Terrace seen in street addresses, sits above MINI in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are the end stations, where trains or buses finish their routes.

clue.text: Doubt expressed in the arboretum?

parts.note: a visitor to a tree collection, unsure which tree is which, might ask out loud which particular elm this is

explanation.surface: Someone voices uncertainty while walking among the trees of a botanical garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The spoken question 'which elm?' sounds just like the name of this tree, the wych elm, so a puzzled visitor's query among the trees names it.
explanation.definitionFit: The wych elm is a native British elm species that you might find in an arboretum.

clue.text: Keen like Peggotty's suitor

definitions.meaning: Barkis, who courts Peggotty in David Copperfield, sends the message 'Barkis is willin''

explanation.surface: Describing someone as eager, just like a Dickens character's admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's David Copperfield, the carrier Barkis proposes to the nurse Peggotty with the famous message 'Barkis is willin''.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ready and eager to do something is the plain sense.

clue.text: Go to Oxford Street for example

definitions.meaning: to ... is to go or travel, as in ... one's way
Oxford Street is a shopping street in London's West End

explanation.surface: Instructions to head to a well-known London shopping street.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford Street is a main shopping street in central London, in the area called the West End; read W (west) plus END.
explanation.definitionFit: To wend is an old word meaning to proceed or travel on one's way.

clue.text: Something to be said for such a test

definitions.text: Something to be said for such a test

parts.words: Something to be said for such a test
parts.note: a spoken examination is one where everything is said rather than written

explanation.surface: Arguing that a particular exam has its merits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something to be said for' is the idiom for 'a point in favour of', but read literally it means the test is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination, as in language exams, is the type of test meant.

clue.text: Ring back about one in time for Kew

indicators.note: about tells us the turned word goes round the single letter
back tells us the word for ring is read in reverse

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Call back a second time to arrange a visit to Kew Gardens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CALL into LLAC, and 'about' places I inside it. The definition echoes Alfred Noyes's poem: 'Go down to Kew in lilac-time'. Kew Gardens is London's great botanic garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Noyes's poem 'The Barrel-Organ' names the season of flowering shrubs as the moment to visit Kew.

clue.text: It is within the law so to abandon petition

indicators.note: to abandon tells us the little word so is dropped from the word for petition

parts.note: to solicit is to petition or ask earnestly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A claim that dropping a petition is perfectly legal.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit is a formal word for lawful or permitted.

clue.text: Sound measure of achievement

indicators.note: sound here means the measure's word is spoken and gives a word that sounds the same

parts.note: feet are a unit of measure

explanation.surface: A reliable gauge of success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but it signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A feat is a notable accomplishment, an exploit requiring skill or courage.

clue.text: Gang reported in town

indicators.note: reported means we want a word that sounds like the word for gang

parts.note: a crew is a gang or team of workers

explanation.surface: A gang was said to be somewhere in the town.
explanation.walkthrough: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewe is a Cheshire railway junction town, an example of an English town.

clue.text: Dostoevsky's character I state to be crazy

parts.note: The Idiot is the title character of Dostoevsky's novel, Prince Myshkin
taken as written
Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone declares a Russian novelist's hero quite mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotical is an old-fashioned form meaning foolish or senseless.

clue.text: Favourable position of Polly Perkins when posing

definitions.meaning: the idiom for being well placed or comfortably off
Polly Perkins of Paddington Green, in the music-hall song, is 'as pretty as a butterfly', so when sitting for a portrait she would be pretty while seated

explanation.surface: A music-hall heroine models for an artist and is well placed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty Polly Perkins of Paddington Green' is a Victorian music-hall song; posing, she would literally be seated and pretty.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being in a comfortable or advantageous situation.
